Date: 2026-04-22
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE) — Jordan Lee (CTO, Nexa.ai), Maria Gonzalez (ML Engineer, Nexa.ai), Samir Patel (VP Product, Nexa.ai), Leah Cho (Security, Nexa.ai)
summary: Demo focused on migration parity from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API. Covered API mapping for completions, chat, function calling, streaming, embeddings; Console rollout for routes and rollouts; Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization) and dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs. Customer requested a parity matrix, security docs, and a benchmark POC.
topics: Redwood Optimize: batching, caching, quantization recommendations
Security: SOC2, KMS, VPC, audit logs
transcript: 00:00 Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Alex, AE at Redwood, and with me are Priya and Diego from our SE team.
00:08 Jordan Lee: Hey, Jordan here. thanks. we're excited to see how close the parity is — we're running a mix of OpenAI and Anthropic across prod and staging, plus some TogetherAI experiments.

00:18 Priya Patel: awesome. high level today we'll walk through API parity, the Console for rollout and monitoring, and our Optimize recommendations for your workload. feel free to stop and ask like you did last time.
00:30 Maria Gonzalez: quick one — streaming and function calling is kinda critical for us, we use functions and partial streaming heavily for UI responsiveness.

00:38 Alex Morgan: totally. we built the parity matrix with that in mind; Redwood supports server-side streaming and chunked tokens, plus function/tool calling semantics that map pretty closely to OpenAI's— slight naming differences in SDK but same flow.

00:52 Diego Ramos: i'm going to share my screen — show the REST examples and a simple node SDK snippet that mirrors your existing calls. (screen share) ok so here's a prompt->chat example using redwood.chat.create — you'll see the examples for function schema and streaming on the right.
01:12 Samir Patel: i see redwood.chat.create, our engineers are mainly using openai.ChatCompletion.create. how heavy is the migration effort?

01:22 Priya Patel: in most cases it's just an adapter layer — endpoint names and param names change but payloads are equivalent. for function calls we map the function json schema directly; we also provide drop-in middleware for express/fastify to translate 90% of calls automatically.
01:40 Leah Cho: security question — KMS, HSM, where does key management live and do you support customer-managed keys?

01:46 Alex Morgan: yes, customer-managed keys via KMS is supported on Private and Dedicated. Hosted API supports envelope encryption and we can sign an SLA addendum; Priya will send the SOC2 and KMS integration notes after the call.
02:00 Maria Gonzalez: embeddings — we use OpenAI's embed endpoint and store vectors in Pinecone. will your embeddings match in dimensionality and semantic behavior?

02:08 Diego Ramos: Redwood offers multiple embedding models, and we've validated interoperability with Pinecone and milvus. there are model family mappings — some semantic shifts exist across models, we recommend running your prompts through our eval harness to choose the best embedding model.

02:28 Alex Morgan: also note the cost/latency tradeoff: some of our quantized variants give huge cost savings for embeddings at a small quality delta — Optimize will suggest the right quant/profile for your workload.
02:39 Jordan Lee: good. latency. our SLO is 200ms for single token streaming on user-facing chat, is that achievable on hosted?

02:46 Priya Patel: with pinned model variants and our GPU routing, many customers consistently hit <200ms median on hosted for small context lengths. Dedicated gives you more predictable p95, and Private lets you tune hardware. we should benchmark with your prompt set.
03:00 Samir Patel: can you do canary rollouts and fallback to openai if a model regresses?
03:04 Alex Morgan: yes — Console supports route-level policies. you can do canary, weighted A/B, and automatic fallback to a specified upstream (including OpenAI) on error thresholds.
03:18 Maria Gonzalez: curious about token accounting and cost reporting per route — we need to attribute spend to products.
03:24 Diego Ramos: Console provides token-level cost breakdowns per route and per model. we have tracing hooks so you can link requests to traces in your systems; that's useful for chargeback.
03:36 Leah Cho: compliance — audit logs retention, SSO/SAML, and RBAC?
03:40 Priya Patel: we support SAML SSO, fine-grained RBAC, and audit logs with configurable retention windows for Dedicated/Private. hosted audit log retention is available as an add-on.
03:54 Jordan Lee: any gotchas moving from TogetherAI? they run some custom quantized models with their runtime.

03:59 Diego Ramos: TogetherAI tends to use some custom kernels; our runtime supports common quant formats and we can onboard custom weights in many cases. there may be kernel compatibility work but it's usually an engineering lift rather than blocker.

04:18 Alex Morgan: i'm going to show a quick parity table — left is OpenAI/Anthropic/Together verb, right is Redwood equivalence. completions -> redwood.completions, chat -> redwood.chat.create, streaming -> \u0018stream parameter, function-calls -> functions param mapping, embeddings -> redwood.embeddings.create.
04:40 Maria Gonzalez: can you demo streaming?
04:42 Priya Patel: yep, quick demo — i'll start a streaming call and you should see partial tokens arrive in the UI. (plays demo) apologies if audio cuts, transcription might miss fragments.
05:05 Maria Gonzalez: looks smooth. how do we handle state/KV cache for long conversations?

05:12 Diego Ramos: Redwood has KV cache management under the hood and we surface APIs for prefix caching; for long convos we recommend checkpointing embeddings and using a context window manager — Optimize can suggest checkpoint intervals.
05:28 Samir Patel: pricing — send us estimated TCO for our 10M token/month baseline and for embeddings-heavy workloads.
05:34 Alex Morgan: will do. we'll include hosted and Dedicated numbers and assumptions about quantization and batching savings.
05:42 Jordan Lee: last question: timeline — if we wanted to pilot, what's typical ramp for a 6-week POC?

05:48 Priya Patel: most POCs are 2-6 weeks depending on benchmarking complexity. given your use of function calls, streaming, and embeddings, i'd budget 4 weeks for migration and a week for run validation.

06:00 Alex Morgan: recap / next steps — i'll send the parity matrix and SDK snippets, Priya will send security/SOC2/KMS notes, Diego will provision a benchmark env and runbook, and Jordan will share representative prompts. we'll aim to kick off week of 05-05.
06:20 Jordan Lee: sounds good, thanks everyone.
06:24 Alex Morgan: thanks, bye.
